docs.title: Deltares MkDocs Template
docs.text:
The Deltares MkDocs Template can be found on GitHub.

This template is based on the Material for MkDocs theme and provides a starting point for creating documentation sites with MkDocs.

The purpose of this template is to provide a consistent look and feel for documentation sites created by Deltares, by providing some style examples and configurations.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• Get started with MkDocs - Get started with the Deltares MkDocs Template.
  • Deltares style guide - Examples showing some Deltares styles.

docs.title: Publishing your site
docs.text:
Detailed instructions on how to publish your site can be found in the MkDocs documentation.

And more specifically, the Material for MkDocs documentation provides instructions on how to deploy your site to different platforms.

docs.title: Running your site locally
docs.text:
Run these commands from the project root, where mkdocs.yml is located. First, create and activate a Python virtual environment, then install Material for MkDocs (which includes MkDocs):

python -m venv .venv

Activate the environment:

# Windows PowerShell
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# macOS or Linux
source .venv/bin/activate

Install the project dependencies:

python -m pip install mkdocs-material

Build the site into the site/ directory:

mkdocs build

To preview the site locally, start MkDocs' development server:

mkdocs serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in your browser. The server rebuilds the site when you save documentation changes; stop it with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Publishing your site
docs.text:
There are different ways to publish your site, depending on the platform you want to use. The most common platforms are GitHub Pages and GitLab Pages.

On the Material for MkDocs documentation you can find instructions on how to deploy your site to different platforms.

Here are some specific instructions for publishing to one of the Deltares supported platforms.

mkdocs gh-deploy --force

docs.title: Deltares supported Pages
docs.text: Deltares offers a number of hosting locations for your documentation site.

docs.title: GitHub
docs.text:
GitHub specific instructions for deploying your site can be found in the GitHub Pages documentation.

The following GitHub pages locations are available for hosting your documentation site:

  • Deltares GitHub Pages - for public documentation sites for the Deltares organization.
  • Deltares Research GitHub Pages - for documentation sites of the Deltares Research organization.

docs.title: GitLab
docs.text:
GitLab specific instructions for deploying your site can be found in the GitLab Pages documentation.

Currently, Deltares does not offer GitLab Pages hosting for documentation sites. However, we are working on providing this in the neer future.

The expected GitLab Pages hosting locations for Deltares documentation sites are:

  • Deltares GitLab Pages - for public documentation sites hosted in the Deltares GitLab instance.
  • Open Deltares GitLab Pages - for public documentation sites hosted in the Open Deltares GitLab instance.

docs.title: MkDocs
docs.text: MkDocs is a static site generator that's geared towards building project documentation. It takes Markdown files and builds a static HTML website from them.

docs.title: Material for MkDocs
docs.text: Material for MkDocs is a theme for MkDocs that provides a modern and responsive design, along with many features and customization options. It is widely used in the MkDocs community and is known for its clean and professional look.

docs.title: Deltares MkDocs Template
docs.text: The Deltares MkDocs Template is an adaptation of the Material for MkDocs theme. It provides stylesheet customizations that offer users a simple way to design project documentation that is consistent in look and feel with Deltares.

docs.title: Markdown Buttons
docs.text:
Markdown does not offer a simple way to create buttons. However the squidfunk mkdocs project does.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these buttons.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the Button styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Buttons */

docs.title: Simple Button
docs.text:
Button

[Subscribe to our newsletter](#){ .md-button }
Subscribe to our newsletter

docs.title: Icon Button
docs.text:
Button with icon

[:fontawesome-solid-arrow-right:](buttons.md){ .md-button }

docs.title: HTML Buttons
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of buttons, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

Below is an example of a button with an icon and text. The button is defined in the deltares.css file under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Buttons */

docs.title: Goto Button (HTML)
docs.text:
Goto Button

<div class="md-group__items"> 
  <div class="md-button md-group__item__button">
    <a  href="#">
        <img alt="arrow right" width="20" height="20"  src="../../assets/arrow-right.svg">
    </a>
  </div>
  <div class="md-group__item__text">
    <a href="#" >
        <h4>Goto</h4>
    </a>
  </div>
</div>
`

Goto

docs.title: Markdown Lists
docs.text:
Markdown offers a simple way to create lists as is shown in the Markdown list reference.

For a more complex reference specifically designed for MkDocs, please refer to the reference in Material for MkDocs.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these lists.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the List styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Lists */

docs.title: Unordered List
docs.text:
Markdown Unordered List
* First item
* Second item
* Third item
____- Subitem 1
____- Subitem 2
________+ Subsubitem 1
________+ Subsubitem 2
  • First item
  • Second item
  • Third item
    • Subitem 1
    • Subitem 2
      • Subsubitem 1
      • Subsubitem 2

docs.title: Ordered List
docs.text:
Markdown Ordered List
1. First item

    ```Add an image.``` ![Deltares logo](./assets/favicon-16x16.png)

2. Second item

    ```Add a code block here to show that the list is still active.```

3. Third item
    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
        1. Subsubitem 1
        2. Subsubitem 2

  1. First item

    Add an image.

  2. Second item

    Add a code block here to show that the list is still active.

  3. Third item

    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
      1. Subsubitem 1
      2. Subsubitem 2

docs.title: HTML List
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of lists, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

The CSS entries for styling the HTML lists are defined in the same section of the deltares.css file as the Markdown lists.:

 /* Deltares overrides for Lists */
HTML Ordered List
<div class="md-typeset__list">
    <ol>
        <li>First item</li>
        <li>Second item</li>
        <li>Third item
            <ol class="md">
                <li>Subitem 1</li>
                <li>Subitem 2
                    <ol>
                        <li>Subsubitem 1</li>
                        <li>Subsubitem 2</li>
                    </ol>
                </li>
            </ol>
        </li>
    </ol>
</div>
  1. First item
  2. Second item
  3. Third item
    1. Subitem 1
    2. Subitem 2
      1. Subsubitem 1
      2. Subsubitem 2

docs.title: Markdown Tables
docs.text:
Markdown offers a simple way to create tables as is shown in the Markdown table reference. More elaborate Table styling options specifically for MkDocs can be found in the squidfunk mkdocs project.

Through the deltares.css stylesheet it is possible to style these tables.

The current styles defined in the deltares.css file are configured according to the Deltares design guidelines.

The entries for the Table styles are can be found in the deltares.css under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Tables */
Markdown Table
| Chart Title      | Euro x1000|Index|
| :----------------| --------: |----:|
| Item 1           | XXX       |XXX  |
| Item 2           | XXX       | XXX |
| Item 3           | XXX       | XXX |
Chart Title Euro x1000 Index Item 1 XXX XXX Item 2 XXX XXX Item 3 XXX XXX

docs.title: HTML Tables
docs.text:
If you wish for more control over the styling of tables, then it is possible to use HTML and CSS.

Deltares supports two colour schemes for tables: Blue (class="md-typeset__table__blue") and Green (class="md-typeset__table__green").

The definitions for these table styles are defined in the deltares.css file under section:

 /* Deltares overrides for Tables */
BlueGreen HTML Table definition
    <table class="md-typeset__table__blue">
        <tr >
          <th align="left">Chart Title</th>
          <th align="right">Euro x1000</th>
          <th align="right">Index</th>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left">Item 1</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left">Item 2</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
          <td align="right">XXX</td>
        </tr>
        <tr >
          <td align="left"><strong>Item 3</strong></td>
          <td align="right"><strong>XXX</strong></td>
          <td align="right"><strong>XXX</strong></td>
        </tr>
    </table>

Chart Title Euro x1000 Index Item 1 XXX XXX Item 2 XXX XXX Item 3 XXX XXX
